title: 第十七章窦氏第十六章连城第十五章鸮鸟
lines: 第十七章窦氏
宋焘看完《连城》，在窗前坐了很久。他想乔生胸口的疤，想连城喝下的那碗腥甜的汤。他想，情到深处，是可以把命给出去的。但情到绝处呢？是不是就会变成恨？他想了很久，想到月亮升起来，又落下去，才闭上眼睛，沉沉睡去。
第二天醒来，他翻开天书。书页自己翻动，停在一页空白上。他等着，等字迹浮现。这一章，叫《窦氏》。
山西临汾有个富家公子，叫南三复。此人家财万贯，良田千顷，生得风流倜傥，一表人才。但他为人轻浮，最是好色，仗着家里有钱，常常在外面沾花惹草。
这一年夏天，南三复去乡下收租。走到半路，忽然下起暴雨。他看见路边有座茅屋，便下马去避雨。茅屋很破，门虚掩着。南三复推门进去，看见一个老头正在编草席，旁边坐着一个年轻女子，低着头做针线。那女子穿着粗布衣裳，头发只用一根荆钗绾着，脸上不施脂粉。但当她抬起头时，南三复心里猛地一跳——那女子生得极美，眉眼如画，皮肤白得像雪，眼神却清澈得像山里的泉水。
老头姓窦，是个佃户。见来了贵人，慌忙让女儿倒茶。那女子叫窦氏，端着茶碗走过来，手有些抖。南三复接过茶碗，指尖碰到了她的手。她的手很凉，像一块玉。
雨下了很久。南三复不走，和窦老头攀谈。他得知窦氏还没许人家，心里便动了歪念头。临走时，他故意留下一锭银子。窦老头不肯收，南三复笑着说：“老人家拿着吧，一点心意。”他上马走了，走了几步，回头看了一眼。窦氏站在门口，扶着门框，正看着他。雨丝飘在她脸上，她的眼睛湿漉漉的，像受惊的小鹿。南三复笑了。他知道，这朵花，他摘定了。
过了几天，南三复又来了。这回他带了一匹绸缎、一盒胭脂。窦老头吓得不敢要，南三复说：“我是看你闺女可怜，一点小礼物，不算什么。”
从那以后，南三复三天两头往窦家跑。他给窦氏带好吃的，带好玩的，说好听的话。他说：“窦儿，你长得这么美，不该埋没在这穷乡僻壤。等我回去跟家里说，一定把你娶进门，做正房夫人。”窦氏是个单纯的农家女，哪里见过这种阵仗？她信了。她觉得南三复是真心喜欢她。她把身子给了他。
那一夜，南三复抱着她，指天发誓：“皇天在上，我南三复若负窦氏，天打雷劈，不得好死！”窦氏信了。她把心掏出来，给了他。
可是，南三复走了，就再也没回来。一天，两天，一个月，两个月。窦氏站在村口的路上等，从夏天等到秋天。路还是那条路，人却不是那个人。她的肚子大了。村里人指指点点，说她不知廉耻。窦老头气得要把她赶出去，她跪在父亲面前哭：“爹，他说他会娶我的。他说他是真心的。”
窦老头不信，拿着棍子去打南家。南家的门房把他打了出来，说：“我们家公子早就订亲了，是城里的曹进士家的小姐。哪来的什么窦氏？别在这里撒野！”窦老头回来，把这话告诉了窦氏。窦氏愣住了。她不信。她说：“不可能，他发过誓的。他说过，若负我，天打雷劈。”
她不相信南三复会骗她。她挺着大肚子，走了几十里路，去城里找南三复。
她到了南家门口。门房拦住她，不让她进。她跪在门口，求门房通报一声。门房进去了一会儿，出来说：“公子说了，他不认识你。让你赶紧走，不然报官抓你。”
窦氏不信。她趴在门缝里往里看。她看见南三复穿着大红喜服，正牵着另一个女人的手，在拜堂成亲。那个女人穿着凤冠霞帔，笑得那么甜。窦氏的心，碎了。
她站在雪地里，看着里面的红灯笼，看着里面的喜字。雪花落在她脸上，化成水，流下来，像眼泪。她抱着肚子，跪在地上，哭不出声。“南三复，”她对着那扇紧闭的大门说，“你骗我。你不得好死。”
那天夜里，窦氏在雪地里生下了孩子。孩子生下来就是死的，浑身青紫，小手紧紧抓着她的衣襟。窦氏抱着死孩子，坐在雪地里，坐了一夜。天快亮的时候，她站起来，抱着孩子，一步一步走回南家门口。她把死孩子放在门口的石狮子旁边，然后自己靠在门上，不动了。
雪越下越大，把她和孩子都盖住了。等到天亮，有人发现她死了。她的眼睛还睁着，死死地盯着南家的大门。那眼神里，没有泪，只有恨。无穷无尽的恨。她的手指抠进了门板的缝隙里，指甲全断了，指尖的肉翻出来，沾着血，冻在木头上。掰都掰不开。
南三复听说窦氏死在他家门口，心里有点怕。但他仗着有钱，花了一千两银子，买通了官府，把这事压了下去。他以为这就没事了。他继续过他的富贵日子。可是，怪事发生了。
新婚的妻子曹氏，本来是个温柔贤惠的女人。但自从窦氏死后，曹氏就变了。她整天不说话，只是坐在窗前发呆。有时候，她会突然笑起来，那笑声很尖，很冷，不像人笑，像鬼哭。她开始半夜起来梳妆，对着铜镜描眉画唇，用的胭脂红得像血。丫鬟问她去哪，她不答，只对着镜子笑。她梳头的姿势也变了，从前是从上往下慢慢梳，现在是从下往上倒着梳，一梳梳到发根，扯下一把头发，也不疼，只是笑。

有一天夜里，南三复起夜，路过曹氏的房门。听见里面有人低声念着什么。他凑近一听，是两句诗：“绣倦慵拈针，日长人静。”他的血一下子凉了。那是窦氏当年绣在《倦绣图》上的句子，他从没告诉过曹氏。他不知道，窦氏死的时候，脑子里最后想的，就是这两句诗。她的怨气太深，死前的最后一个念头，像钉子一样钉在了虚空里。曹氏离她最近，那念头就钻进了曹氏的梦里，一点一点地啃噬她的魂魄，把她的模样、她的习惯、她的恨，全都灌进了曹氏的身体里。
有一天夜里，南三复喝醉了酒，回到房里。曹氏坐在床上，背对着他。“娘子，睡吧。”南三复说。曹氏慢慢转过身来。南三复一看，吓得魂飞魄散——那不是曹氏的脸，那是窦氏的脸！她的脸惨白惨白的，眼睛红红的，嘴角流着血。她怀里抱着一个青紫色的小孩，那小孩正冲着他笑。
“南三复，”那“东西”说，“你看，我们的儿子来看你了。你抱抱他。你从来没有抱过他。”
那小孩伸出手，指甲又长又黑，朝南三复的喉咙抓来。南三复尖叫一声，晕了过去。

Chapter 17 Dou Family
After Song Tao finished watching "Linked City", he sat in front of the window for a long time. He missed the scar on Qiao Sheng's chest and the bowl of fishy-sweet soup that Liancheng drank. He thought that if you were deeply in love, you could give up your life. But what about reaching the end of love? Will it turn into hatred? He thought for a long time, thinking about the moon rising and setting, before closing his eyes and falling asleep.
When he woke up the next day, he opened the Book of Heaven. The pages of the book turned by themselves and stopped on a blank page. He waited for the writing to appear. This chapter is called "Dou Family".
There was a rich man named Nan Sanfu in Linfen, Shanxi Province. This man has a fortune, thousands of hectares of fertile land, and a handsome and talented person. But he is frivolous and most lecherous. He often indulges in promiscuity outside because of his family's wealth.
This summer, Nan Sanfu went to the countryside to collect rent. Halfway through, it suddenly started raining heavily. He saw a thatched hut on the roadside and dismounted to take shelter from the rain. The hut was very dilapidated and the door was ajar. Nan Sanfu pushed the door open and went in. He saw an old man weaving a straw mat, and a young woman sitting next to her, her head lowered and doing needlework. The woman was wearing coarse clothes, her hair was only tied with a thorn hairpin, and there was no makeup on her face. But when she raised her head, Nan Sanfu's heart skipped a beat - that woman was extremely beautiful, with picturesque features, skin as white as snow, and eyes as clear as spring water in the mountains.
The old man's surname was Dou, and he was a tenant farmer. Seeing the noble man coming, he hurriedly asked his daughter to pour tea. The woman's name was Mrs. Dou, and she came over with a tea bowl, her hands shaking a little. Nan Sanfu took the tea bowl and touched her hand with his fingertips. Her hand was cold, like a piece of jade.
It rained for a long time. Nan Sanfu stayed away and talked with Old Man Dou. When he learned that Mrs. Dou had not married anyone yet, he had a strange thought in his heart. Before leaving, he deliberately left a piece of silver behind. Old Man Dou refused to accept it, so Nan Sanfu smiled and said, "Take it, old man, for a little thought." He mounted his horse and walked away. After walking a few steps, he looked back. Mrs. Dou stood at the door, holding on to the door frame, looking at him. Raindrops floated on her face, and her eyes were wet, like a frightened deer. Nan Sanfu smiled. He knew that he was sure to pick this flower.
A few days later, Nan Sanfu came again. This time he brought a piece of silk and a box of rouge. Old Man Dou was too frightened to ask for it. Nan Sanfu said, "I just feel sorry for your daughter. A small gift is nothing."
From then on, Nan Sanfu ran to Dou's house every two days. He brought delicious food and fun things to Mrs. Dou, and said nice words. He said: "Dou'er, you are so beautiful, you shouldn't be buried in this remote place. When I go back and tell my family, I will definitely marry you and make you the first wife." Mrs. Dou is a simple peasant girl. Where has she seen such a battle? She believed it. She felt that Nan Sanfu really liked her. She gave her body to him.
That night, Nan Sanfu held her in his arms and swore to the sky: "God above, if I, Nan Sanfu, betray the Dou family, I will be struck by lightning and die badly!" Dou family believed it. She took out her heart and gave it to him.
However, Nan Sanfu left and never came back. One day, two days, a month, two months. Mrs. Dou stood on the road at the entrance of the village and waited from summer to autumn. The road is still the same road, but the person is not the same person. Her belly is getting bigger. People in the village pointed fingers and said she was shameless. Old Man Dou was so angry that he wanted to drive her out. She knelt in front of her father and cried: "Dad, he said he would marry me. He said he meant it."
Old Man Dou didn't believe it and went to beat the Nan family with a stick. The concierge of the Nan family beat him out and said, "Our young master has been engaged for a long time. He is the daughter of Cao Jinshi's family in the city. Where did Mr. Dou come from? Don't act wild here!" Old Man Dou came back and told Mr. Dou this. Dou was stunned. She didn't believe it. She said: "It's impossible, he swore an oath. He said that if you betray me, the sky will strike like lightning."
She didn't believe that Nan Sanfu would lie to her. With a big belly, she walked dozens of miles to find Nan Sanfu in the city.
She arrived at the door of Nan's house. The concierge stopped her and refused to let her in. She knelt at the door and begged the concierge to inform her. The concierge went in for a while and then came out and said, "The young master said that he doesn't know you. I want you to leave quickly, or the police will arrest you."
Mr. Dou didn't believe it. She lay on the crack in the door and looked in. She saw Nan Sanfu, wearing a bright red wedding dress, holding another woman's hand and getting married in the church. That woman was wearing a phoenix crown and a hare, and she smiled so sweetly. Dou's heart was broken.
She stood in the snow, looking at the red lantern inside and the word "happy" inside. Snowflakes fell on her face, turned into water, and flowed down like tears. She hugged her belly and knelt on the ground, unable to cry. "Nan Sanfu," she said to the closed door, "you lied to me. You will not die well."
That night, Dou gave birth to her child in the snow. The child was born dead, covered in bruises, and her little hands were tightly grasping the skirt of her clothes. Dou held the dead child in his arms and sat in the snow all night. When it was almost dawn, she stood up, held her child in her arms, and walked back to the door of Nan's house step by step. She placed the dead child next to the stone lion at the door, and then leaned against the door, motionless.
The snow fell harder and harder, covering her and the child. When daybreak, someone found her dead. Her eyes were still open, staring at the door of Nan's house. There were no tears in those eyes, only hatred. Endless hate. Her fingers dug into the cracks in the door panel, and her nails were completely broken. The flesh of her fingertips was turned out, stained with blood, and frozen on the wood. Can't even be broken apart.
Nan Sanfu was a little scared when he heard that Mrs. Dou died in front of his house. But relying on his wealth, he spent a thousand taels of silver to bribe the government and suppressed the matter. He thought it would be okay. He continued to live his wealthy life. However, something strange happened.
The newlywed wife Cao was originally a gentle and virtuous woman. But since Dou's death, Cao has changed. She didn't speak all day long, just sitting in front of the window in a daze. Sometimes, she would laugh suddenly. The laughter was sharp and cold, not like human laughter, but like a ghost crying. She began to get up in the middle of the night to put on her makeup, and painted her eyebrows and lips in front of the bronze mirror. The rouge she used was as red as blood. The maid asked her where she was going, but she didn't answer and just smiled in the mirror. The way she combs her hair has also changed. She used to comb it slowly from top to bottom, but now she combs it backwards from bottom to top. She combs it to the root of her hair and pulls out a handful of hair. It doesn't hurt, she just smiles.
One night, Nan Sanfu got up at night and passed by Cao's house. I heard someone inside whispering something. When he got closer, he heard two lines of poetry: "I am tired of embroidering, and I pick up the needle lazily, but the day is long and people are still." His blood suddenly ran cold. That was a sentence that Mr. Dou had embroidered on the "Tired Embroidery Picture" back then, but he never told Mr. Cao. He didn't know that when Mr. Dou died, the last thing he thought about was these two lines of poetry. Her resentment was too deep, and her last thought before her death was like a nail stuck in the void. Cao was the closest to her, and that thought entered Cao's dream, biting away at her soul bit by bit, pouring her appearance, her habits, and her hatred into Cao's body.
One night, Nan Sanfu returned to his room drunk. Ms. Cao sat on the bed with her back to him. "Madam, go to sleep." Nan Sanfu said. Ms. Cao slowly turned around. When Nan Sanfu saw it, he was frightened to death - that was not Mr. Cao's face, that was Mr. Dou's face! Her face was pale, her eyes were red, and her mouth was bleeding. She held a purple child in her arms, and the child was smiling at him.
"Nan Sanfu," the "thing" said, "look, our son comes to see you. You hug him. You have never hugged him before."
The child stretched out his hand, with long and black nails, and scratched at Nan Sanfu's throat. Nan Sanfu screamed and fainted.
